clock.none: No source: no plan for the day
clock.set: Controller's clock set from this browser ({time})

alert.hotspot: The controller isn't on any Wi-Fi network: you are on its hotspot « {ssid} ».
alert.no_clock: The controller doesn't know the time: it can't compute today's plan.

wifi.join_failed: Couldn't join « {ssid} » (password or range). The controller keeps its network.
wifi.join_hint_hotspot: The controller tries this network for 30 s and saves it only if the connection succeeds. Once connected, its hotspot stops: join that network with this phone, then open {url}.
wifi.join_hint: The controller tries this network for 30 s and saves it only if the connection succeeds; otherwise it keeps the current network. If it changes network, this page loses the link: find it again at {url}.
wifi.pw_short: Password: 8 characters at least, or empty for an open network.
wifi.confirm_switch: The controller will leave « {from} » for « {to} ». This page will lose the link: find it again at {url}. Continue?

fw.rebooting: Controller restarting on the new version…
fw.installing: Installing {version}… The controller then restarts (about 1 min).
fw.pending_fill: {version} will install when the running fill ends.
fw.pending_override: {version} will install when the forced speed ends.
fw.error_check: The check failed: no network, or no version published yet.
fw.up_to_date: Up to date: {installed} is the latest version.
fw.not_checked_every: Not checked yet: the controller checks every {every}.
fw.confirm_install: Install {version}? The controller downloads it, installs it and restarts (about 1 min); the pump then resumes its plan. During a forced speed or a fill, it waits for them to end.
fw.auto_sub: A version found by the periodic check installs by itself, after a forced speed or a running fill. One found with “Check” waits for “Install”.
fw.interval_sub: The controller asks GitHub for the latest published version.

inst.done: {version} installed: the controller restarted on it.
inst.wait_fill: Waiting for the running fill to end.
inst.wait_override: Waiting for the forced speed to end.

log.heading: Log
log.title: Controller messages
log.none: No line yet. The controller only sends the messages logged while the page is open (level INFO and above).

login.title: Log in
login.hint: The one chosen at setup. This browser then stays logged in; after 6 h without use, the page asks again.
login.no_answer: The controller doesn't answer: try again in a moment.
login.locked: Too many attempts: try again in {wait}.

waiting.pool_temperature: a reading from the pool probe

pw.others_relog: Other devices will have to log in again with it; this one does so by itself.
pw.not_confirmed: The controller didn't confirm the password.
pw.page_changed: Page password changed: the other devices will have to log in again.

pos.rounded: Rounded to 0.01° (about 1 km): enough for the sun, without locating the house. North and east are positive. On a map, a long press on the pool gives its coordinates.
pos.browser_unlisted: This browser is on {zone}, not in the list: pick a zone with the same time, or type its POSIX string (the “TZ” column of the time zone database).
pos.name_display: The name is only for display; the controller applies the POSIX string.
pos.keeps_both: The controller keeps both: {zone}, which it shows, and the POSIX string it applies, {posix}.
pos.sun_intro: With the latitude and the longitude, the controller computes sunrise and sunset, from which it places the filtration.
pos.polar_day: With these values, today: polar day. Check the latitude's sign.
pos.polar_night: With these values, today: polar night. Check the latitude's sign.
pos.sun: With these values, today: sunrise {rise}, sunset {set}. If they are far from yours, check the signs and the time zone.
pos.bad_degrees: Latitude between -90 and 90, longitude between -180 and 180, in decimal degrees.
pos.bad_name: Time zone name: Zone/City, like Asia/Kolkata.
pos.tz_refused: The controller refused this time zone: its POSIX string doesn't pass its parser.
pos.not_confirmed: The controller didn't confirm the position.
pos.from_ha: Or from Home Assistant: Pool card › Controller settings › Position.

probes.scanning: Looking for probes on the 1-Wire bus…
probes.none: No probe answered on the 1-Wire bus. Check the wiring, then run the detection again.
probes.hint: To tell them apart, hold one in your hand: within a minute it gains a few degrees. {pool} (on the filter's return) is required, the plan and freeze protection depend on it; the other two are optional.
probes.moved: {role}: probe {probe}; {previous} no longer has a role

fill.heading: Water meter

untested.sub: “Test”, then open the fill tap: it needs {litres} L in {minutes} min.

listening.sub: Open the fill tap: {litres} L in {minutes} min is enough.

detected.sub: It counts: a fill was seen.

not_detected.sub: Less than {litres} L in {minutes} min: check the wiring, then run the test again.

fill.off_toast: Water meter off: nothing is counted
fill.listening_toast: Listening: open the fill tap ({litres} L in {minutes} min)
fill.switch_aria: Water meter on the fill line
fill.on_sub: It counts the water added (Control › Filling) and raises an alarm if a fill runs too long.
fill.off_sub: Nothing is counted: no Filling, no alarm. For a pool without a meter on its fill line.
fill.alarm_sub: A longer fill sets off the alarm: here, and Home Assistant reminds every 15 min until “Acknowledge”. 0 = never.
fill.alarm_bad: Alarm after: a number of minutes, from {min} to {max}
fill.wz_none_sub: Nothing is counted. To add one: Controller settings › Water meter.
fill.wz_detected_sub: It counts: Filling and its alarm are in place.
fill.wz_intro: A pulse meter on the fill line (1 L per pulse): the controller counts the water added, and raises an alarm if a fill runs too long.

ha.title: Encryption key
ha.step1: In Home Assistant: Settings › Devices & services. The controller shows up by itself, “Discovered”: ESPHome, Pool Controller (otherwise: “Add integration” › ESPHome › pool-controller.local).
ha.step2: Add, then confirm. Home Assistant generates the key and sends it to the controller: nothing to copy, nothing to keep.
ha.waiting_sub: This page updates as soon as the key is set.
ha.open_note: As long as no key is set, any device on the network can talk to the controller: add it now.
ha.paste_hint: For a controller Home Assistant already knows (a migration: the api_encryption_key value of the old secrets.yaml): it reconnects with it, changing nothing. Until then, don't confirm “encryption removed” in Home Assistant.
ha.key_invalid: Invalid key: 32 bytes in base64, that is 44 characters ending in “=”.
ha.key_saved: Key saved: Home Assistant reconnects with it.
ha.key_gen_failed: The controller couldn't give itself a key.
ha.key_generated: Without Home Assistant: random key set
ha.forget_failed: The controller didn't forget its key.
ha.forgotten: Key forgotten: add the controller in Home Assistant
ha.key_unset_sub: Home Assistant sets it when it adds the controller.
ha.state_waiting_sub: Add the controller in Home Assistant: it sets the key itself.
ha.by_paste: Pasted on this page (migration). Never shown again.
ha.by_generated: Random, drawn by the controller: nobody knows it, nobody needs it.
ha.by_ha: By Home Assistant, when it added the controller. Shown nowhere, neither here nor in Home Assistant.
ha.by_unknown: The controller never shows it, here or anywhere else.
ha.state_linked_sub: It talks with the controller, encrypted with this key.
ha.state_unused_sub: The controller works on its own: plan, freeze protection and updates.
ha.state_unlinked_sub: Without Home Assistant, that's normal: the controller works on its own. To add it there, it must first forget its key.
ha.forget_hint: The controller forgets its key and waits for Home Assistant, which will set one when adding it (Settings › Devices & services). Until then, any device on the network can talk to it: do it right away.

acc.heading: Access
acc.title: Passwords
acc.page_sub: This page asks for it to open, then each browser stays logged in until 6 h without use. It also protects the hotspot, which stays open.
acc.ota_sub: To send a firmware from a computer (make ota). Drawn at random at first start until you choose one; updates from this page and Home Assistant don't need it.
acc.write_only: Write-only: the controller never shows them, it only says whether they are set.
acc.logout_hint: “Log out”: this page will ask for the password again here.
acc.logout_all_hint: “Log out all devices”: each will have to give it again, this one included. For a lost, or lent, phone.

restart.heading: Restart
restart.title: Restart the controller
restart.row_sub: Keeps everything. The pump stops during the restart (about 30 s), then the controller resumes in Auto: a forced speed ends.
restart.confirm: Restart the controller now? This page reconnects by itself.

reset.heading: Reset
reset.title: Factory settings
reset.row_sub: Erases the access, the Wi-Fi and the key; keeps the probes, the position and the time zone, so the plan and freeze protection.
reset.wiped_key: the encryption key: Home Assistant loses the link.
reset.kept_probes: the probes' roles, the position and the time zone: the filtration plan and freeze protection carry on;
reset.kept_settings: the settings (filtration, freeze protection, water meter, updates) and the history kept here (last 7 days, filling);
reset.after: The controller restarts on its hotspot “{ssid}”, open: connect a phone to it and open http://192.168.4.1. The setup only asks again for what was erased: a password, the Wi-Fi, then Home Assistant.
reset.toast: Reset: the controller erases its access and restarts…

wz1.after_reset: This controller was reset. It kept its probes' roles, its position and its time zone: the filtration plan and freeze protection carry on. It needs {needs} again.
wz1.new: This controller is fresh from the factory: nothing is set yet. Five steps, a few minutes, and everything stays on the controller.
wz1.hotspot: Its hotspot “{ssid}” is open, with no Wi-Fi password: this page's password is what protects the controller. Choose it first; until there is one, anyone who joins the hotspot can open this page.
wz1.hint: 8 characters at least. This page will ask for it to open, and the controller will never show it again: keep it in your password manager.
wz1.set: Password set. Leave empty to keep it.
wz1.choose: Choose a password for this page.

wz2.hotspot_off: The controller turned its hotspot off: this page no longer reaches it here.
wz2.hotspot_will_stop: Once connected, the controller turns its hotspot off: this page no longer reaches it here.
wz2.reconnect: Reconnect this phone to the Wi-Fi “{ssid}”.
wz2.resume: The page asks for the password of step 1. Then it reads Setup State and resumes at the first missing step: {step}.
wz2.change_later: To change network later: Controller settings › Wi-Fi.
wz2.connecting_sub: Up to 30 s; if it fails, the hotspot stays.
wz2.hotspot_sub: This phone is connected to the controller itself. Open hotspot: this page, for its part, has its password.
wz2.intro: Choose the home network: the controller connects to it, then turns its hotspot off. It needs one: the time comes to it from the Internet, and Home Assistant goes through it.
wz2.lose_link: This page then loses the link; reopened on the home network, it resumes where it was (Setup State keeps {item} until then).

wz3.intro: The controller places the filtration from sunrise and the afternoon's heat: it needs the pool's position and the local time.

found.one: {count} probe found on the bus. Give each one a role:
found.other: {count} probes found on the bus. Give each one a role:

wz4.need_pool: Give at least the pool probe.
wz4.not_confirmed: The controller didn't confirm the pool probe.

wz5.intro: Home Assistant talks to the controller encrypted. It creates the key itself: add the controller there, it generates the key and sends it over.
wz5.not_home: The controller isn't on the home network yet (step 2): Home Assistant can't reach it.
wz5.after_reset: Home Assistant knew this controller with the old key: it reports “encryption removed” on the device. Confirm: it sets a new one by itself.
wz5.pasted: Pasted from the old secrets.yaml: Home Assistant reconnects with it.
wz5.generated: The controller gave itself a random key that nobody sees. To add it later: Controller settings › Home Assistant.
wz5.by_ha_sub: It is connected, encrypted. The key is shown nowhere.
wz5.unlinked: The controller has its key. Home Assistant isn't connected for now: Controller settings › Home Assistant.

done.plan2: Today's plan is computed: {hours} h, {block1} and {block2}.
done.page_sub: This page asks for it to open
done.ha_generated: Random key; Controller settings › Home Assistant to add it.

setup.banner: The controller isn't set up yet: it needs {needs}.
